sources_considered.why: Reports ARC-AGI-3 launch scores for frontier models, including Claude Opus 4.6, which was current at the post date.
Primary description of what ARC-AGI-3 measures (novel environments, acquiring goals on the fly).

Software-task horizons. More relevant to the long-horizon claim; used there.

receipt.public_excerpt: Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro led the pack at 0.37%. OpenAI’s GPT-5.4 came in at 0.26%. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6 managed 0.25%, while xAI’s Grok-4.20 scored exactly zero. Humans, meanwhile, solved 100% of environments.

evidence_items.explanation: On a benchmark built to test generalization in novel environments, frontier systems from the period (including Claude Opus 4.6, released before the post) scored under 1%. Humans solved every environment. This is a large shortfall on the speaker's named standards.

receipt.public_excerpt: drop an AI agent into an unfamiliar game-like world with zero instructions, zero stated goals, and no description of the rules. The agent has to explore, figure out what it's supposed to do, form a plan, and execute it.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows the test targets the same abilities the claim names: generalization under novelty and autonomous goal-directed behavior.

receipt.public_excerpt: challenges AI agents to explore novel environments, acquire goals on the fly, build adaptable world models, and learn continuously.

evidence_items.explanation: Primary description of the benchmark's design, which matches the claim's criteria.

evidence_items.publisher: Nature (Comment by Chen, Belkin, Bergen, Danks)

receipt.public_excerpt: The vision of human-level machine intelligence laid out by Alan Turing in the 1950s is now a reality.

evidence_items.explanation: Some experts argued at the time that human-level general intelligence had already arrived. This is an opinion piece, not a measurement, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: The evaluations that decide this were published in March 2026, a few weeks after the post. They test systems that were current at the post date, but some of the models scored (GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro) were released after it.
No single agreed measure exists for 'original AGI standards'.
